back.title: Back and shoulders
back.intro: The acupoints are marked on the picture with their names. Tap a name to see where the point is and what it is often stimulated for.
back.note: Most points come in pairs, one on each side of the spine. Both sides are stimulated.

items.name: Dazhui
items.where: On the middle of the spine, in the dip just below the bump at the base of the neck. The bump is easy to feel when you bend your head forward.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for a stiff neck and tension in the upper back.

items.name: Jianjing
items.where: On the top of the shoulder, halfway between the base of the neck and the tip of the shoulder.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for tight, aching shoulders.

items.name: Fengmen
items.where: On the upper back, about two finger-widths either side of the spine, level with the top edge of the shoulder blades.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for tension in the upper back and shoulders.

items.name: Feishu
items.where: On the upper back, two finger-widths either side of the spine, between the shoulder blades, a little below Fengmen.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for tightness between the shoulder blades.

items.name: Tianzong
items.where: In the middle of the shoulder blade, in the hollow below the ridge that runs across it.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for an aching shoulder blade and a stiff shoulder.

items.name: Xinshu
items.where: Two finger-widths either side of the spine, level with the middle of the shoulder blades.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for an achy, tight mid-upper back.

items.name: Geshu
items.where: Two finger-widths either side of the spine, level with the bottom tip of the shoulder blades.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for a tight mid-back.

items.name: Ganshu
items.where: Two finger-widths either side of the spine, a little below the bottom tip of the shoulder blades.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for an achy mid-to-lower back after sitting for long.

items.name: Pishu
items.where: Two finger-widths either side of the spine, just above the waist.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for stiffness just above the waist.

items.name: Shenshu
items.where: At waist level, two finger-widths either side of the spine, level with the navel.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for a tired, aching lower back.

items.name: Mingmen
items.where: On the middle of the spine at waist level, in the dip between the two Shenshu points.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for a stiff, cold or tired lower back.

lines.label: Governor line (督脉)
lines.text: Runs up the middle of the spine, from the tailbone to the head.

lines.label: Bladder line (膀胱经)
lines.text: Two lines about two finger-widths either side of the spine. Most of the points here sit on them.

press: Your therapist first guides the device along the meridian, then rests the probe on each key point.
The probe gives gentle pulses and warmth. Most people feel a light tingle or a comfortable warmth.
The strength is raised slowly. Tell your therapist right away if anything feels uncomfortable.
A little soreness or warmth afterwards is normal. Rest and drink some water.
back.cautionIntro: Ask your therapist or doctor first, and do not use the device, if you:
caution: are pregnant or may be pregnant
have a pacemaker or any implanted electronic device, or a metal implant in the area
take blood-thinning medicine or bruise easily
have a recent injury, fracture, surgery or swelling in the area
have osteoporosis, a spine problem or nerve pain
have a skin problem, wound or sunburn on the area
back.cautionNote: Never use the device on broken skin, a lump or a swollen, red or painful area.
doctor: Sudden, severe back pain, or pain after a fall or injury
Numbness, tingling or weakness in the arms or legs
Back pain with a fever, or trouble controlling your bladder or bowels
Pain that wakes you at night, or that has not eased after 2 weeks
back.warnLine: Pain spreading to the chest, arm or jaw, trouble breathing, or sudden weakness on one side? Call 999 now.

items.name: Lungs and chest
items.where: Upper back, across both shoulder blades, one lung area on each side of the spine.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for a tight chest and shallow breathing from stress.

items.name: Heart
items.where: Middle of the upper back, just to the left of the spine, between the shoulder blades.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe to feel calm and relaxed.

items.name: Liver and gallbladder
items.where: Right side of the mid-back, just below the shoulder blade, over the lower ribs.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for tiredness and a heavy feeling after rich meals.

items.name: Stomach, spleen and pancreas
items.where: Left side of the mid-back, below the shoulder blade, over the lower ribs.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for a bloated or unsettled stomach after meals.

items.name: Kidneys and adrenals
items.where: Lower back, one on each side of the spine, just above the waist.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for a tired lower back and heavy, tired legs.

items.name: Intestines

back_probe.intro: For therapists: the steps of a neck, shoulder and back session, in order. Tap a step to see where the probe goes.
back_probe.note: Steps 1 to 5 follow a neck and shoulder routine and steps 6 and 7 a lower back routine. Hands, arms, buttocks and legs are not on this picture.

items.name: Shoulder tops
items.where: On the top of both shoulders, around Jianjing, along the edge of the shoulder.
items.uses: Glide the probe slowly along the edge of the shoulder, forward and back, then repeat on the other side.

items.name: Shoulder blades
items.where: Along the inner edge of each shoulder blade, around Tianzong.
items.uses: Rest the probe on the sore spots along the inner edge of each shoulder blade, one spot at a time.

items.name: Base of the neck
items.where: On the spine, in the dip just below the bump at the base of the neck (Dazhui).
items.uses: Rest the probe here for a short hold.

items.name: Spine, upper back
items.where: Down the middle of the spine, from the base of the neck to between the shoulder blades.
items.uses: Glide slowly down the middle of the spine from the base of the neck, then back up, and repeat.

items.name: Upper back, beside the spine
items.where: On both sides of the spine, around Fengmen and Feishu.
items.uses: Rest the probe on each of these points in turn, left and right.

items.name: Lower back
items.where: The lower back: down the middle of the spine, then down the lines on each side of it.
items.uses: Glide slowly down the middle of the spine, then down each line beside it, from the top and from the inside outward.

items.name: Sides of the waist
items.where: Around the waist on both sides, along the belt line.
items.uses: Glide the probe around the waist from front to back and back again, and rest it for a moment on any tight knots.

foot_points.intro: Points on the sole and toes that lie on the meridians. Tap a name to see where it is.
foot_points.note: The toe points sit beside the corners of the toenails and the heel points just below the ankle bones, so they are drawn at the edges of the foot. Your therapist finds the exact spot.

items.name: Yinbai
items.where: On the inner side of the big toe, right beside the corner of the toenail.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for cold, tired toes.

items.name: Dadun
items.where: On the outer side of the big toe (the side facing the second toe), right beside the corner of the toenail.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for an achy, tired big toe.

items.name: Zhiyin
items.where: On the outer side of the little toe, right beside the corner of the toenail.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for tired, achy little toes and the outer edge of the foot.

items.name: Yongquan
items.where: On the sole, about a third of the way back from the toes, in the dip between the pads below the second and third toes (the dip shows when you curl your toes).
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for tired, aching soles and heavy legs.

items.name: Rangu
items.where: On the inner edge of the foot, in the arch, just in front of and below the bony bump on the inner side of the foot.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for an aching, tired arch.

items.name: Zhaohai
items.where: On the inner side of the heel, in the dip just below the inner ankle bone.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for tired ankles and heavy legs.

items.name: Shenmai
items.where: On the outer side of the heel, in the dip just below the outer ankle bone.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for tired ankles and a stiff lower back.

foot.title: Foot map
foot.intro: Reflexology is a traditional idea that the sole of the foot is a map of the body. Tap an organ to see where its area is on the foot.
foot.note: The heart area matters most on the left foot, and the liver area on the right foot. Your therapist usually works on both feet.

items.name: Head and brain
items.where: The pad of the big toe.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for a tired head, tension headaches and a busy mind.

items.name: Sinuses
items.where: The tips of all the toes.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for a blocked or heavy feeling around the nose and forehead.

items.name: Eyes
items.where: The base of the middle toes, where they meet the ball of the foot.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for tired, strained eyes after screen time.

items.name: Ears
items.where: The little toe, towards its base.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for a blocked-ear feeling and tension around the ears.

items.name: Neck and thyroid
items.where: The base of the big toe, just below the toe pad.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for a stiff neck and a tight throat.

items.name: Lungs and chest
items.where: The ball of the foot, on both sides of the heart area.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for a tight chest and shallow breathing from stress.

items.name: Heart
items.where: The middle of the ball of the foot, between the lungs. It matters most on the left foot.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe to feel calm and relaxed.

items.name: Liver and gallbladder
items.where: Just below the ball of the foot, on the outer side. It matters most on the right foot.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for tiredness and a heavy feeling after rich meals.

items.name: Stomach
items.where: Just below the ball of the foot, on the inner (big-toe) side.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for a bloated or unsettled stomach after meals.

items.name: Pancreas
items.where: Just below the stomach area, on the inner side.
items.uses: Often stimulated together with the stomach area for digestion comfort.

items.name: Intestines
items.where: The lower arch, from just below the liver and stomach areas down to the heel. The large intestine runs around the small intestine.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for bloating and digestion comfort.

items.name: Kidneys and adrenals
items.where: The heel, on the outer (little-toe) side, with the adrenal gland on top.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for a tired lower back and heavy, tired legs.

items.name: Bladder
items.where: The heel, on the inner (big-toe) side, next to the kidney area.
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for a heavy or uncomfortable lower belly.

items.name: Spine
items.where: The whole inner edge of the foot, from the big toe (neck) to the heel (lower back).
items.uses: Often stimulated with the probe for a stiff, tired back.

good: This is a traditional map. Studies have not proven that foot areas are linked to organs, and most people use reflexology to relax.
A sensitive spot does not mean there is a problem with that organ.
Feeling relaxed or a little sleepy afterwards is common.

foot_probe.intro: For therapists: the steps of a sole session, in order. Tap a step to see where the probe goes.
foot_probe.note: These are the sole steps of the leg routine. The calf, buttock and lower back steps are on other pictures.

items.name: Centre of the sole
items.where: The dip in the front part of the sole, below the second and third toes (Yongquan).
items.uses: Start here: rest the probe flat on the sole with light contact and make small circles.

items.name: Toe joints
items.where: Along the row of joints at the base of the toes, across the ball of the foot.
items.uses: Glide the probe in short straight strokes and small circles along the toe joints, gently, a few passes on each foot.

items.name: Closing stroke toward the heel
items.where: Down the middle of the sole, from the toes to the heel.
items.uses: To finish, glide slowly from the toes toward the heel and ankle, in the direction of the heart.

cupping.title: Cupping marks
cupping.intro: Cupping uses gentle suction on the skin. It leaves round marks where the cups sat. They look like bruises, but they come from the suction drawing blood to the skin surface, not from an injury to the muscle. Most marks fade within 1 to 2 weeks.
cupping.guideTitle: What the colours can look like
cupping.guideSub: Your marks may be lighter or darker than these. Every person's skin reacts differently.

stages.name: Light pink
stages.look: A faint, pale mark. The suction was gentle or short, or your skin does not mark easily.
stages.tip: Usually gone within a few days.

stages.name: Light red
stages.look: A mild, even mark. A very common result.
stages.tip: Usually fades within a few days to a week.

stages.name: Red to dark pink
stages.look: A clear, medium mark. The suction was firmer, or the cups stayed on a little longer.
stages.tip: Usually fades in about a week.

stages.name: Deep red to purple
stages.look: A strong mark. Firm suction, a longer time, or skin that bruises easily.
stages.tip: Can take 1 to 2 weeks. Tell your therapist so the next session can be gentler.

stages.name: Dark purple to black
stages.look: A very deep mark. It may feel tender to touch.
stages.tip: Can take 2 weeks or more. Tell your therapist right away and ask for lighter suction or a shorter time next time. See a doctor if it is very painful or is not fading after 2 weeks.

stages.name: Fading yellow, green or brown
stages.look: The healing stage. The mark is fading, just like an ordinary bruise does.
stages.tip: Be gentle with the skin until it is back to normal.

good: The colour is not a health test. It mostly shows how strong the suction was, how long the cups stayed on, and how easily your skin marks.
Some people mark more easily than others. Light marks, or very few, are normal too.
You may feel a little tight or slightly sore for a day or two. It should not be severe.
care: Keep the area clean and dry. Do not scrub, scratch or pick at it.
Skip very hot showers, saunas and hard workouts for the rest of the day.
Keep the marks out of strong sun until they fade.
Drink water and rest if you feel tired, dizzy or light-headed.
If the skin feels dry or tight, a gentle fragrance-free moisturiser is fine.
Wait until the marks have faded before the same spot is cupped again, and ask your therapist how long to leave it.
cupping.cautionIntro: Tell your therapist, and check with your doctor first, if you:
caution: are pregnant, under 18, or older and frail
take blood-thinning medicine, or have a bleeding or blood-clotting problem
have anaemia, heart disease or a pacemaker
have epilepsy
have eczema, psoriasis or another skin problem
have sunburn, a wound, a burn, thin or inflamed skin, or varicose veins in the area
cupping.cautionNote: Cups should never be placed on broken, burnt or infected skin.
cupping.doctorTitle: When to tell your therapist or see a doctor
doctor: Blisters, a burn, or skin that is broken or oozing
Fever, spreading redness, warmth, or yellow discharge (signs of infection)
Severe pain or swelling that gets worse instead of better
Marks that are not fading after 2 weeks, or you bruise easily or often for no reason
Feeling faint, dizzy or sick, and it does not settle after lying down
cupping.warnLine: Feeling very unwell, fainting, or chest pain or trouble breathing? Call 999 or go to the nearest emergency department now.
cupping.refs: Cleveland Clinic, Healthline, WebMD, NCBI StatPearls
